## 3B.10 Research Note: Kishida in 2024

Overall read: **mostly yes, but only partially and unevenly**. Kishida’s 2024 record shows real gains in disaster response, evacuation, resilience, and rights-protective messaging, which plausibly left ordinary citizens safer from preventable domestic harm. The main counterweight is that Japan’s criminal-justice abuses and arbitrary detention practices clearly persisted, so the safety picture was not uniformly improved.

- **Instructions by the Prime Minister Regarding the Earthquake Centered in Ishikawa Prefecture** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 1, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/decisions/2024/0101shiji.html) | Kishida ordered timely public warnings, evacuation, damage prevention, and emergency disaster response with human life first. This is direct evidence that he tried to reduce deaths and injuries from a major domestic crisis. | `3B.10`, `3B.9`

- **Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 11, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/11kaiken.html) | He urged secondary evacuation for people at higher risk, including elderly people, infants, nursing mothers, and disabled people, to protect life and health and reduce disease and overcrowding in shelters. This is strong evidence of safety-oriented crisis management. | `3B.10`, `3B.7`, `3B.9`

- **Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the Package of Measures to Support the Daily Lives and the Livelihoods of the Disaster Victims and Other Matters** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 25, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html) | Kishida said the government had shifted from immediate response to restoring infrastructure and “peaceful livelihoods” for disaster victims. That supports a finding that he worked to reduce displacement and lingering insecurity after the quake. | `3B.10`, `3B.9`

- **People feeling safe and well-assured in their daily lives** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 page content | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/safety.html) | The cabinet’s own policy summary says the government’s mission is to protect lives and assets from disasters, aging infrastructure, infectious disease disasters, and public-safety risks. This is programmatic evidence of a safety-first governing posture. | `3B.10`, `3B.9`

- **Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Symposium on Inclusive Society and Human Rights** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 5, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html) | Kishida explicitly rejected unfair discrimination and violence against foreigners, people with disabilities, Ainu people, and sexual minorities, tying policy to human dignity and the rule of law. That is relevant positive evidence for broader domestic safety and social stability. | `3B.10`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`

- **Video Message from Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio on International Women’s Day** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 8, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/08message2.html) | Kishida pledged action against sexual crime and sexual violence, and support for survivors and victims, including women facing compounded difficulties. This is direct evidence of reducing preventable harm to a vulnerable group. | `3B.10`, `3B.7`

This is evidence of restrained crisis communication rather than panic or militarized spectacle. | `3B.10`, `3B.9`

- **Inquiry Needed into Japan’s Flawed Criminal Justice System** | Human Rights Watch | November 4, 2024 | [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/04/inquiry-needed-japans-flawed-criminal-justice-system) | HRW used the Hakamada case to argue that Japan’s justice system still produced extreme wrongful-punishment outcomes and needed inquiry and reform. This is stronger negative evidence that structural domestic insecurity persisted during Kishida’s term. | `3B.10`, `3B.8`

### Search gap
I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence of large-scale political violence, communal violence, or protest crackdowns in Japan under Kishida. The evidence base instead centers on disaster response, rights protection, and the persistence of structural criminal-justice abuse. That means the main negative side is **not** state terror or mass repression, but **unfinished institutional harm** in detention and prosecution.
